ORDINANCE NO. __ of 2019
AN ORDINANCE PROVIDING MINIMUM ENERGY STANDARDS FOR THE DESIGN OF NEW
BUILDINGS AND STRUCTURES OR PORTIONS AND ADDITIONS TO EXISTING BUILDINGS THAT
PROVIDE FACILITIES OR SHELTER FOR PUBLIC ASSEMBLY, EDUCATION, BUSINESS,
MERCANTILE, INSTITUTUIONAL, STORAGE, AND RESIDENTIAL OCCUPANCIES, AS WELL AS
THOSE PORTIONS OF FACTORY AND INDUSTRIAL OCCUPANCIES DESIGNED PRIMARILY FOR
HUMAN OCCUPANCY BY REGULATING THEIR EXTERIOR ENVELOPES AND THE SELECTION
OF THEIR HVAC, SERVICE WATER HEATING, ELECTRICAL DISTRIBUTUION AND
ILLUMINATING SYSTEMS AND EQUIPMENT FOR EFFECTIVE USE OF ENERGY; AND FOR
OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, more efficient buildings can conserve energy, reduce stress on our electricity grid
and natural gas supplies while saving money and resources for our citizens; and
WHEREAS, improved building codes emphasizing energy conservation can reduce future energy
consumption and the costs associated with energy production; and
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE
CITY OF CABOT, ARKANSAS:
SECTION 1: ADOPTION OF ENERGY CODE. There is hereby adopted by the City Council of
Cabot Arkansas, for the purpose of establishing rules and regulations for energy efficient standards for new
building construction, this Code known as the 2014 Arkansas Energy Code, being particularly the 2014
Arkansas Energy Code edition thereof and the whole thereof, save and except such portions as are
hereinafter deleted, modified, or amended, of which not less than three (3) copies of this ordinance, as well
as, three (3) copies of the 2014 Arkansas Energy Code, have been and now are filed in the office of the City
Clerk~Treasurer, and the same ordinance is hereby adopted and incorporated as fully as if set out at length
herein, and from the date on which this ordinance shall take effect, the provisions thereof shall be controlling
in the construction of all buildings and structures therein contained within the corporate limits of the City of
Cabot, Arkansas.
SECTION 2: The City Council of Cabot, Arkansas further requires Heat and Air duct testing as
follows:
(1) New Residential Construction. Duct testing shall be required for all new single-family residential
structures. Single-family residential developments that utilize the exact same floor plan multiple times
are required to have duct testing completed on a minimum of 20% of new single-family residential units.
(2) New Multi-Family Construction. Duct testing shall be required for all new multi-family developments
and shall meet the following testing criteria when these developments utilize the exact same floor plan.

a. Two (2) units up to 200 units shall have a minimum of 20% of units tested and certified. This
includes individual floors with 200 units or less per floor. This includes individual buildings
where the total numbers of units are less than 200 units for the entire building.
b. 201 units and up shall have a minimum of 10% of units tested and certified. This includes
individual floors that exceed 201 units or more per floor. This includes individual buildings
where the total number of units exceeds 201 units or more.
c. In cases where the development is a continuous building completely connected, the number
of units shall be determined where required Fire Tenant Separation Walls are installed.
d. If the development utilizes the same HVACR contractor for the duration of construction the
rules for testing 10% or 20% shall be granted. In cases where another HVACR Contractor is
hired prior to completion of the project, the project regardless of the number of units shall
meet the 20% testing criteria up to completion.
(3) Addition, Alterations and Renovations. Additions, alterations and renovations to existing residential
structures shall not be required to comply with the duct testing requirements, but shall be required to
comply with the 2014 Sr. Energy Code and 2010 AR Mechanical Code Duct Sealing Requirements.
(4) Repairs. All repairs to existing residential structures and mechanical systems shall not be required to
comply with the duct testing requirements, but shall be required to comply with the 2014 AR Energy
Code and 2010 AR Mechanical Code duct sealing requirements.
(5) Duct Tester Qualifications. The duct tester shall be certified by one (1) of the following:
a. Residential Energy Services Network Certified Rater (RSNET) or equivalent
b. Building Performance Institute Certified Rater (BPI)
c. AR HVACR Association Certified Duct Tester
Duct Testing Criteria:
Duct Testing shall be verified by either of the following:
(1) Rough-In Test: Total leakage shall be less than or equal to 6 cfm (169.9L/min) per 100 ft² (9.29m²)
of conditioned floor area when tested at a pressure differential of 0.1 inches w.g. (25 Pa) across the
roughed in system, including the manufacturer’s air handler enclosure. All register boots shall be
taped or to otherwise sealed during the test. If the air handler is not installed at the time of the test,
total leakage shall be less than or equal to 4 cfm (113 L/min) per 100 ft² (9.29m²) of conditioned
floor area.
(2) Post Construction Test: Leakage to outdoors shall be less than or equal to 8 cfm (226.5 L/min) per
100 ft² (9.29m²) of conditioned floor area or a total leakage less than or equal to 12 cfm (12 L/min)
per 100 ft² (9.29m²) of conditioned floor area when tested at a pressure differential of 0.1 inches
w.g. (25Pa) across the entire system, including the manufacturer’s air handler enclosure. All register
boots shall be taped or otherwise sealed during the test.
Exceptions: Duct tightness test is not required if the air handler and all ducts are located within
conditioned space.

(3) Duct Testing Compliance and Verification: The tester shall provide (City-provided form) within
five (5) days of completion to the Building Codes Division, the results of the test and that the duct

testing complies with Section 2. A Certificate of Occupancy shall not be issued without completion
verification and compliance with the duct testing requirements.
SECTION 2: REPEALER. Ordinances or parts thereof in force at the time that this ordinance shall
take effect, if inconsistent herewith, are hereby repealed.
SECTION 3: EMERGENCY CLAUSE. Whereas it is of the utmost urgency that the city of

,

Arkansas, have an up-to date Energy Code to protect the citizens of our city, therefore, an Emergency is hereby
declared to exist and this ordinance being necessary for the immediate protection of the public shall take effect
immediately on its passage and approval.

ORDINANCE NO. __OF 2019
AN ORDINANCE TO CREATE AN EXEMPTION ELECTRONIC FENCES IN THE
CITY OF CABOT; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
WHEREAS, it is the desire of this governing body to allow electronic fences within the
City of Cabot.
NOW THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS, THAT:
SECTION 1: The City of Cabot hereby adopts an exemption for electronic fences
delineated as follows:
A.

Electronic Fence Exemption.
1.
Definition of "electronic fence": An electronic fence is a fence that
controls the movement of a dog by emitting an electrical shock through an
electric collar worn by the dog when the dog nears the boundary of the
property around which the fence is located.
2.

Filing of Application for Exemption.
a)
An application for an exemption must be filed with the
Office of Animal Control by the dog owner (applicant) and must
legally reside where the fence is to be located.
b)
The application must be filed in the form the Animal
Control requires.

3.

Contents.
a)

The application must:
(1)
Be accompanied by the site plan for the electronic
fence, including the property lines, dimensions and existing
structures.
(2)
Include a written statement by the applicant, with
adequate supporting evidence, showing how the applicant
will conform to the following standards:
(a)
The fence shall be installed in such a way that
the dog confined shall not come within ten (10) feet of
any public footpaths, walkways, allies or streets.
(b)

The fence shall not be installed closer than

five (5) feet from an adjacent property.
(3)

Provide proof that the animal is neutered or spayed.

(4)
Include a statement by the applicant that the
applicant:
(a)
understands that approval of the fence in no
way relieves the applicant of responsibility for control
of his/her dog and any damages caused by his/her dog;
and
(b)
continues to accept responsibility for the dog
and its actions, including any damages to the dog, the
applicant, and third parties resulting from the applicant's
dog, and the use of an electronic fence
to contain the dog.
4.

Posting of Property.
a)
Applicant's property must be posted for ten (10) consecutive
days immediately upon the filing of the application for an exemption.
b)

Sign Placement.
(1)
The posted sign must be placed in a conspicuous
area, not over ten (10) feet above the ground and clearly
visible and legible to the public
(2)
The posted sign shall not be less than four (4) feet long
and three (3) feet high with black block lettering not less than
two (2) inches high on a white background.

c)

Content.
(1)
The sign must state the applicant has requested an
exemption from Animal Control to install and maintain an
electronic fence and specify the species of dog the fence is to
confine.

5.

Approval or Denial of Application for Exemption.
(1)

HEARING PROCEDURE REGULATIONS
I.

DEFINITIONS
A.
Aggrieved Party – The party aggrieved by a notice, order, decision, or other
action of the Office of Animal Control. This may include the owner or custodian of
an animal and/or the complainant.
B.
Chairperson – The Mayor of the City of Cabot or his/her designee will
administratively preside over the Panel as a non-voting member.
C.

Department – This is the Cabot Animal Services.

D.
Hearing Record – All objects, documents, attendance records and recorded
testimony admitted into evidence at the hearing and the attendance roll taken at
the hearing.
E.
Interested Party – This is a person who is personally or
specifically affected by the outcome of the hearing.
F.
Office of Animal Control – This is the Office of Animal Control in the
Department.
G.
Panel – The member(s) of the Compliance Committee who act as hearing
officer(s). This will include the Chairperson, Director of Animal Services or
his/her designee, Director of Municipal Services or his/her designee, and
Planning Commission Chairman or his/her designee.
H.
Party – The Office of Animal Control, Aggrieved Party, or an
Interested Party.
II.

NOTICE OF HEARING
A.
A hearing shall be scheduled by the Panel within a reasonable time after a
proper request for a hearing is received from the Aggrieved Party.

1

B.
At least 5 days before the hearing, the Panel must provide notice of the
hearing to the Aggrieved Party and any Interested Party. The Panel shall notify
the Aggrieved Party and any Interested Party\ via written notification.
C.

The written notice must state:
1.

The date, time, place, and nature of the hearing;

2.
The right of a Party to call witnesses and submit documents or
other evidence; and
3.
That failure to appear for the scheduled hearing may result in
an adverse action against the Party.
III.

HEARING OBJECTIVES
A.

The objectives of the hearing are to make written:
1.

Proposed or final findings of fact;

2.

Proposed or final orders; or

3.

The final administrative decision of the Department.

B.
On the question of whether an application for exception of electronic
fence was justly denied, the Panel must determine, based on the facts
presented:
1.

2.

Whether the application is:
a)

Is denied;

b)

Is incomplete; or

c)

Is neither denied nor incomplete; and

d)

Meets criteria for approval

What, if any, corrective action is appropriate?

2

IV.

HEARING GENERALLY
A.
Any hearing pertaining to the determination of whether an application was
justly denied of 3 members of the Panel. The Chairperson shall administer the
activities of the Panel.
B.
The hearing shall be open to the public unless the Panel votes to conduct a
closed hearing or to seal portions of the Hearing Record for any reason that a
public court hearing, trial or other processing may be closed or sealed.
C.
A Panel may determine who shall be deemed an Interested Party at the
hearing.
D.
The Panel shall make an audio recording of the hearing and compile and
label the Hearing Record. Said recording shall be considered official audio of the
hearing. Unless permitted by the Panel, no additional audio, video or other
recording shall be made of the hearing.
E.
Any time during the proceedings, but prior to the issuance of a final
decision and/or order, the Panel may inspect any relevant premises. All Parties
present at the hearing shall have reasonable notice of the inspection, and shall
be given the opportunity to be present during the inspection.

V.

PANEL MEMBER’S RESPONSIBILITIES
A Panel is responsible:
A.

to conduct the hearing in an orderly manner.

B.

to obtain relevant evidence from all Parties.

C.
to provide the Parties with the opportunity to present their case in an
orderly manner, to call witnesses on their behalf, to cross-examine all other
witnesses, and to establish any pertinent facts.
D.
to admit all relevant testimony, objects and documents, and to compile
the Hearing Record. Any Party may examine any object or document prior to
its introduction into evidence.
E.
to make written findings and render a decision and/or order based
upon the Hearing Record and any inspection.

3

VI.

ORDER OF HEARING
A.
The Panel shall begin the hearing with a statement concerning the purpose of
the hearing and the procedure that it will follow.
B.
The Panel shall give all persons present at the hearing the opportunity to
register their full name and address on a sign-in sheet, regardless of whether the
person wishes to testify or be considered a Party.
C.

A Party must represent himself/herself.

D.

A Party may make an opening statement.

E.
The Panel may question any witness at any time, and may call any
individual as a witness.
F.
A Party may testify on his/her own behalf, and is subject to crossexamination by other parties.
G.

A Party may make a closing argument.

H.

Opening statements and closing arguments are not considered evidence.

I.
Notwithstanding the procedures herein, the Panel may, in its discretion,
decide the order in which testimony and evidence shall be presented.
J.
In the discretion of the Panel, the hearing may be postponed or
continued.
VII.

RULES OF EVIDENCE
A.
The Panel may admit and give probative effect to evidence which possesses
probative value commonly accepted by reasonable and prudent people in the
conduct of their affairs.
B.
Formal rules of evidence and formal trial procedures shall not apply to the
hearing, except as provided in these procedures. The Panel may not exclude
evidence solely on the basis that it is hearsay.
C.

The Panel shall give effect to the rules of privilege recognized by law.

D.
Documentary evidence may be admitted in the form of copies or excerpts,
or by incorporation by reference.
E.
The Panel may take administrative notice of facts of a general, technical
or scientific nature.
4

F.
The Panel may exclude incompetent, irrelevant, immaterial, or unduly
repetitious evidence.
VIII. DECISIONS AND ORDERS
A.
The Panel shall make written final decision that contains separate statements
of the findings of fact, conclusions of law, the decision and/or order within thirty
(30) calendar days of the termination of the hearing.
B.
The Panel shall mail or deliver a copy of the written decision to each
Party or that Party’s attorney of record.

furnaces or electric baseboard heaters. The label shall include the completion date, builder company name and
the license number assigned by the Arkansas Contractor's Licensing Board. The label will serve as an indication

RESOLUTION NO. 13 OF 2019
A RESOLUTION DESIGNATING THE CITY OF CABOT AS A PURPLE HEART
CITY; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
WHEREAS, first created as the Badge of Military Merit by George Washington in
1 772, the Purple Heart is the oldest military decoration presently in use, and
WHEREAS, The Purple Heart was the first American service award or decoration made
available to the common soldier and is specifically awarded to any member of the United States
Armed Services wounded or killed in combat with a declared enemy of the United States, and
WHEREAS, many former residents of Cabot have made the ultimate sacrifice in giving
their lives in the cause of freedom, and numerous combat-wounded veterans currently reside
within this city and contribute to this community in countless ways, and
WHEREAS, chartered by an act of Congress, the mission of the Military order of the
Purple Heart is to foster an environment of good will among the combat-wounded veterans and
the veteran members and their families, promote patriotism, support legislative initiatives and
most important, make sure we never forget, and
WHEREAS, we appreciate the sacrifices our Purple Heart recipients have made in
defending our freedoms and believe it is important that we acknowledge them for their courage
and show them the support they have earned, and
WHEREAS, the City of Cabot wishes to pledge its strong support to the Military Order
of the Purple Heart and for those who put their lives at risk in service of their country and their
fellow citizens,
NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS THAT:
SECTION 1: The City Council of the City of Cabot, Arkansas does hereby proclaim
that Cabot, Arkansas is a "PURPLE HEART CITY."
SECTION 2: This resolution shall be in full force and effect from and after the date of
its passage.

Cabot City Council Work Session
Cabot City Annex / Council Chambers
March 4, 2019
6:30 p.m.
The Cabot City Council held its monthly Work Session on Monday, March 4, 2019 in the City Annex Council
Chambers. Council Members present were: Ed Long, James Reid, Kevin Davis, Damon Bivins, Matt
Webber, Ronald Waymack, Doug Warner and Norma Naquin. Others present: Mayor Kincade, City
Attorney Jim Taylor, and City Clerk & Treasurer Tammy Yocom.
Ed Long, Chairman of the Public Works Committee, called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m.
Municipal Services: (Ed Long)
1. Harmful Structures Report by Joe Gunderman – Per Ed, this report was given to the Municipal
Services Committee during their meeting on February 21, 2019. Joe gave an overview of the
printed report in the packet. Discussion. Joe will need to work with the City Attorney’s office and
have a solution to review in the April Municipal Services Committee meeting and the council
meeting in May, per Ed Long. No action. Mayor Kincade stated he was looking forward to some
direction.
2. Building Permit Fees – Norma announced the legislation increasing permit fees since they have
not been increased since 1996. Joe explained the proposal found in the packet offering a new fee
structure. Discussion. Mr. Jay O’Neal (local builder) was in attendance and spoke in opposition
of raising permit fees but suggested the increase be phased in if an increase was approved.
Discussion on why builders are not building in Cabot, but they are in Ward and Austin. It was
mentioned that having low permit fees does not draw builders to Cabot, since it was established
that builders want to build elsewhere and we currently have low permit fees. Discussion. It was
determined there was a bigger issue. Norma stated this topic should go back to the Municipal
Services Committee in April (18th) for further review. It was determined the Mayor and Joe would
have open communication (some type of meeting) with the builders in town and work out some
of the day to day issues that the council does not need to be involved with. Norma asked Joe to
bring another suggestion regarding fees to the April 18th MSC meeting. It was suggested the Home
Builders Association be notified of any meetings builders can attend. Motion by Kevin to hold all
action until after the MSC meeting on April 18th when the subject could be revisited, second by
James. Motion passed with a unanimous voice vote.
3. Contract to Sell ARDOT – Mayor Kincade asked the council to be aware of this necessary sale and
the details would be coming to them for the March council meeting. Travis Young announced he
was checking on the warranty of the sign that needs to be moved.
Fire Award – Josh Henson was awarded the Medal of Heroism by Fire Chief, Phil Robinson.
4. Invisible Fence Proposed Legislation – This is a complex issue that needs more time and attention
before the council votes on it, per Ed. Discussion. Mike Wheeler explained this was a citizen driven
issue now and it was when invisible fences were banned in 2014. Mayor Kincade urged the council
to allow this because of all the people in Greystone that have electric fences. He also stated, if we
wanted to be an economic friendly city, we would want to allow some sort of electric fence.
Motion by Kevin to hold all action until after the MSC meeting on April 18th when the subject
could be revisited, second by James. Motion passed with a unanimous voice vote. Mayor Kincade
advised Mike Wheeler, Animal Services Director, that until this is resolved he and his staff should
educate citizens by letting them know the law, where we are at in changing it, and what we are
looking at doing, but no fines.

115

Community Development: (Kevin Davis)
1. Uncommon Communities- Becky Williams presented a PowerPoint presentation. A copy is
attached to these minutes. No action
2. Community Development Input – Amy Williams announced Energy is installing automated meters
for faster service and Master Gardeners is looking at maintaining the welcome signs and also Main
Street Streetscape grassy areas.
3. General Community Input –None
Budget & Personnel: (Doug Warner)
1. Budget Amendment – Mayor Kincade said he was approached by senior citizens about having a
covered area to keep out of the elements when walking between buildings. They have received
quotes ranging from $16,000 to $50,000 and would like to complete this project. Joe Gunderman
stated he would like to go with a local company, Windows and More. Mayor Kincade stated they
are a client of Kincade & Company. Kevin Davis asked City Attorney, Jimmy Taylor, if this was a
conflict of interest and Jimmy stated it was not. Doug Warner stated he was on the Board of the
Lonoke County Council on Aging and, according to their guidelines, it was not a conflict of interest
for him to vote on this. Motion by Kevin to place item on this month’s council meeting agenda,
second by Damon. Motion passed with a unanimous voice vote.
2. Organize Military Relations Committee – There are no dates or times scheduled for this
committee at this time, per Doug. Matt, James, Ron, and Norma agreed to be on this committee

3. State Legislature Representation – Discussion regarding letting Doug represent the City of Cabot
at the State Legislature meetings. Mayor Kincade stated Mr. Hill and Mr. Evans (State Senators)

DECLARING AN EMERGENCY; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
WHEREAS, Arkansas Code Annotated § 14-234-214 provides that the rates for
customers of a municipal waterworks system shall be fixed by the legislative body of
the municipality; and
WHEREAS, The City of Cabot, Arkansas (the “City”) has delegated responsibility
for the operations of the water and wastewater systems to the Cabot Water and
Wastewater Commission (the “Commission” or “Utility”); and
WHEREAS, The City desires that the Commission provide wastewater services
to customers that do not currently receive the Commission’s water services; and
WHEREAS, The Commission has requested that the City establish the schedule
of rates to be charged by the Commission for wastewater services for customers that
receive the Commission’s water services and those that do not receive its water
services and to equitably allocate the Utility’s general and administrative costs
amongst its water and wastewater customers.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE
CITY OF CABOT, ARKANSAS THAT:
Section 1. Purpose. It is the purpose of this Ordinance to establish a policy
allowing the Cabot Water and Wastewater Commission to provide wastewater
services to properties to customers that do not receive its water services, to fix fair and
reasonable wastewater rates and fees applicable to customers of the Cabot Water and
Wastewater Commission, and to equitably allocate the Utility’s general and
administrative costs amongst its water and wastewater customers.

who does not pay his or her bill prior to the close of the regular business day on the
Cut-off Date will be Disconnected and may be Locked-off. Any customer whose water
service meter has been Disconnected or Locked-off by the Utility will be assessed a
Re-connection fee in addition to any and all past-due amounts, penalties, and fees. No
customer shall be reconnected unless and until all past-due amounts, penalties, and
fees, including the Re-connection fee, have been paid in full.
B.

Account Termination. When an account becomes delinquent for

30 days, the Utility shall mail notice to the location receiving service notifying the
customer that the delinquent account is being terminated. If payment is not received
within 10 days, the Utility may terminate the delinquent account and liquidate the
customer’s deposit to offset any and all debts owed to the Utility. The Utility may

1726099-v1

6

initiate collection procedures according to Arkansas law to collect any outstanding
debts remaining after application of the deposit. Any customer whose account has been
terminated due to non-payment may be required to pay an increased deposit to reestablish service.
C.

Insufficient Checks. All returned checks or insufficient funds

drafts will be charged a check service fee as allowed by Arkansas law. If not timely
paid, action will be commenced under the Arkansas Hot Check Law and the service
disconnected.

All fees and assessments as set forth in this Ordinance or any

amendment thereto shall be applied. If two returned checks or drafts are received on
an account for 2 consecutive months, a letter will be mailed to the customer stating
that only certified funds or cash will be accepted for a period of one (1) year.
D.

Billing Malfunctions. In the event of a computer hardware or

software failure or other circumstances beyond the control of the Utility, the
Commission shall have full discretion to extend the Due Date and Cut-off Date for a
period of time commensurate with the delay of the monthly billing or late notice
processing.
Section 9. Billing Disputes. Billing disputes may be initiated by any customer
by contacting the Utility. Upon receipt of a billing dispute, the Utility shall perform
an investigation to compile relevant facts. Upon completing the investigation, the
Utility shall compile a synopsis of the facts, all findings of its investigation, and all
documents submitted by the complainant and forward the same to the Chairperson of
the Commission for a final decision.

1726099-v1

After considering all relevant information
7

presented by both the Utility and the complainant, the Chairperson, or the
Chairperson’s designee, shall render a decision regarding the proper amount of the
bill.
Section 10. Cooperation with Other Service Providers.

Where

necessary, for any Non-Water Customer or Non-Water Customer – With Trash, the
Utility is authorized to cooperate with the water-service provided for any Non-Water
Customer or Non-Water Customer – With Trash to carry out the purposes of this
Ordinance.
Section 11. Severability.

The provisions of the Ordinance are hereby

declared to be separable and if any provision shall for any reason be held illegal or
invalid, such holding shall not affect the validity of the remainder of the Ordinance.
Section 12. Repealer.

All parts of previous Ordinances and Resolutions in

conflict herewith are hereby repealed.
Section 13. Other Unaffected Policies.

Unless

in

conflict

with

the

Ordinance, all other Ordinances, Resolutions, and Utility policies will be unchanged.
Section 14. Declaration of Emergency.

The proper and beneficial use of

water and wastewater and the providing of water and wastewater services to the City
of Cabot are of great importance to the welfare, health, and safety of the inhabitants
of the City of Cabot. It is therefore declared that an emergency exists, and this
Ordinance being necessary for the immediate preservation of the public peace, health,
and safety shall be in full force and effect from and after its passage.

Growing up in a family of entrepreneurs, Mitchell Ward always had a desire to create opportunities for
himself. While growing up in Jacksonville he spent most of his time working alongside his father, Dennis
Ward, learning the ins and outs of the family business at their dealership, City Motors. Mitchell
graduated from Jacksonville High School in 1997. He went on to major in Business Administration at
Southwestern Assembly of God University in Waxahachie, Texas. Mitchell has always valued hard work
and dedication.
After working for himself through college and several years after, he joined his dad in business at City
Motors. Shortly after that, they established Red River Dodge in Heber Springs. Under Mitch's leader
ship Red River grew to become the #1 Ram dealer in the state of Arkansas in a town of less than 7,000
people. With their success, Chrysler asked them to open an additional store in Malvern, this was the
beginning of Red River of Malvern. Around 2012, when Cypress Creek Golf Course was threatened with
going out of business, Mitch partnered with other community members to invest in it. Mitch's goal for
this golf course was to have a family friendly atmosphere for the community and today the golf course is
thriving. In 2018 Mitch began looking for ways to expand his business. He found a great opportunity to
purchase a Dodge Chrysler Jeep Ram Franchise in Quincy, Fl., Coastal Jeep Ram (sadly it's not on the
coast)!
Mitch is a family man first. He has been married to his wife Jessica for 15 years and they have three
beautiful children: Caden, Drake, & Adalyn. Mitch and Jessica have called Cabot home for over 14 years
now. He has coached local kids softball, baseball, flag football, and basketball (2019 boys 7-9 th grade
champs).
He has been a member of McArthur Church in Jacksonville for 30 years. Although he has always served
the church in different capacities, he now serves on the church board as a Deacon. Governor Hutchison
nominated Mitch to serve on the Motor Vehicle Commission, where he is currently a Commissioner. He
has also been nominated by several of his business peers to serve on the Arkansas Auto Dealer
Association as well as the FCA Dealer Council.

Special Community and Economic Development Work Session
Cabot City Annex / Council Chambers
May 14, 2019
7:00 p.m.

The Cabot City Council held a special Work Session on Tuesday, May 14, 2019 in the City Annex Council
Chambers. Council members present were: Ed Long, Matt Webber, Kevin Davis, Damon Bivins, James Reid,
Ronald Waymack, Doug Warner and Norma Naquin. Others present: Mayor Kincade, City Attorney Jim
Taylor, and City Clerk/Treasurer Tammy Yocom.

Council Member Kevin Davis opened the meeting at 7:00 p.m.

Community Development (Kevin Davis)

1. Arts & Entertainment District - Mayor Kincade addressed the council advocating for an
Arts and Entertainment District as defined by the checkered area in the attached map.
He asked that no one get confused with this request as it is not in conjunction with
Arkansas ACT 812 allowing for open alcoholic drinks in a designated district. Discussion.
It was determined ACT 812 is for wet counties only and, since Lonoke is a dry county, open
container would be against the law. There was much discussion on the size, name,
planning the area, zoning and future zoning and change to current land owners within the
area. It was determined the priority of tonight’s meeting is designating a downtown area
and an Arts and Entertainment District for planning and growth purposes and could easily
be modified in the future. Council members and everyone in attendance were given the
opportunity to ask Mayor Kincade questions regarding this proposal. Motion to place this
legislation regarding an Arts and Entertainment District on the May’s Council Meeting
Agenda by Norma, second by Matt. Motion passed with a vote of 7-1. Ron Waymack
voted no.

2. Economic Development Business Incentives — Kevin Davis announced it was not unheard
of for cities to offer incentives to attract businesses to the area. Mayor Kincade wanted
the public’s and council members’ thoughts on providing a small monetary incentive to
the downtown businesses to spruce up their outside areas. This would be paid out of his
$65,000 community and economic development budgeted amount for 2019. Mayor
Kincade asked what could be done to get existing businesses excited about growth and
asked for the Council's input. Kevin reiterated that this meeting was for brainstorming
and a workshop to determine where everyone was on this incentive issue. Getting
everyone up to code is a simple first step, per Norma. She also is bringing an alcohol tax
proposal to the May Municipal Services/Budget and Personnel Committee Meeting that
could possibly be “ear marked” for community and economic development. Discussion
on what types of businesses Cabot is looking for. Discussion on what Cabot should offer
to new businesses. A member of the audience spoke in favor of Mayor Kincade’s idea of
offering an incentive to existing businesses. No action.

3. Cabot WaterWorks - Mayor Kincade stated that he and Amy need to know from an
economic development standpoint what they can offer to restaurants or businesses as
far as water/wastewater and/or hook ups. The Mayor stated he respects WaterWorks as
a separate autonomous commission but is seeking a partnership so that he and Amy will
know in advance of meetings with future businesses what is allowable for them to offer.
Discussion. Tim Joyner stated so many of the old laws forbid donating property or material
but their attorney is looking into it. No action.

--- page 2 (OCR) ---
4. Economic Development Quarterly Report — Presented by Amy Williams. Discussion. A
copy is attached to these minutes. No action.

5. Community Development Input — Becky Williams, owner of Rebecca Williams
Photography and Vice-President of Cabot Foundation for Arts and Culture addressed the
council in support of the Cabot Foundation for Arts and Culture. No action.

The meeting was adjourned at 8:35 by a unanimous vote.

WHEREAS, this ordinance does not waive the competitive bidding requirements of

as amended, to obtain up to 3 quotes for purchases in excess of $1,000 but less than $20,000.

ARKANSAS, THAT:
SECTION 1:

Louis Cimino is hereby permitted to conduct business with the City of

Cabot, Arkansas, as described, upon the approval of this governing body.

SECTION 2: This Ordinance only gives authority for the services delineated on Exhibit
"A", attached hereto and incorporated herein by this reference, and for none other. The authority
for the given herein applies only to that activity which is specifically permitted and is the extent
of the approval of that authority for the time period referenced herein.

SECTION 3: This Ordinance does not waive any requirements enacted by state or city
law concerning competitive bidding.

SECTION 4: This Ordinance shall be in effect for two years from the date of its
passage.

SECTION 5: REPEALER: All ordinances/resolutions and parts of ordinances and/or
resolutions in conflict herewith are hereby repealed.

WHEREAS, the 2014 Arkansas Energy Code provides minimum energy standards for the
design of new buildings as well as additions to existing buildings, specifically residential and
commercial facilities intended for human occupancy, by regulating their exterior including
HVACR, Service Water Heating, Electrical Distribution, illuminating systems and equipment for
the effective use of energy; and
WHEREAS, pursuant to A.C.A § 14-55-206 and 207, the City of Cabot has published
notice in a local newspaper that the City Council will consider enacting an ordinance to adopt
and require all new residential construction and renovations to comply with the 2014 Arkansas
Energy Code, three copies of which are available for public inspection and review in the Cabot
City Clerk Treasurer's Office.

CITY OF CABOT, ARKANSAS:
SECTION 1: That the City Council of the City of Cabot, Arkansas enacts 2014 Arkansas
Energy Code as a whole thereof:

SECTION 2:

Chapter 6, Article II § 6.19 - Adoption of codes is hereby

amended to reflect that the 2014 Arkansas Energy Code has been adopted by reference.

Arkansas, have an up-to date Energy Code to protect the citizens of our city, therefore, an
Emergency is hereby declared to exist and this ordinance being necessary for the immediate
protection of the public shall take effect immediately on its passage and approval.

CENTRAL ELEMENTARY SIDEWALKS – PHASE II
Project Narrative
The City of Cabot has worked diligently over the past several years to develop safe pedestrian
routes along key corridors around the city. The primary goal has been to connect residential
areas with high use public areas such as schools, parks, commercial areas, and various
municipal buildings. Below is a partial list of the projects undertaken by the city over the past 7
years and their function:
Central Elementary Sidewalk Extension – Phase I (2019-Under Construction):
Sidewalk Improvements connecting Central Elementary to surrounding residential area it serves.
Magness Creek SRTS (2015):
Sidewalk Improvements & Pedestrian Bridge to connect North & South Magness Creek to Magness Creek
Elementary School.
Hwy 89 Streetscape (2014):
Sidewalk Improvements along Hwy 89 that connected the Main Street Corridor to existing sidewalks downtown.
N 2nd & Hwy 89 Intersection (2014):
Improved pedestrian route at Main St intersection adjacent to City Hall
E Main, E Elm, & S Lincoln SRTS (2013):
Sidewalk improvements adjacent to Eastside Elementary School & Cabot High School connecting facilities into
existing pedestrian systems.
Hwy 89 & Campground Crosswalk (2012):
Sidewalk & Crosswalk improvements providing a safe crossing route of Hwy 89 (S Pine St) adjacent to the
Campground Corridor.
First Street Sidewalk, Phase I (2012):
Sidewalk Improvements along the First Street Corridor connecting several partial segments of sidewalks installed
by adjoining subdivisions and Westside Elementary.
Hwy 89 Streetscape, Phase II (2017):
Sidewalk Improvements along Hwy 89 that continue Phase I to 10 th Street.
First Street Sidewalk, Phase II (2017):
Sidewalk Improvements along First Street connecting Phase I to a large residential area (Pheasant Run
Subdivision).

Phase II of the Central Elementary Sidewalk Project will not only expand the residential area
served by Phase I, but also provide critical connections to existing sidewalks on South Pine
Street (Hwy 89), South Lincoln, Ivanhoe Drive, Sycamore Street, and Plaza Drive. The
interconnection of this phase provides continuity of pedestrian sidewalks from a high use
commercial area at Plaza & Hwy 89 through Central Elementary area to the City Municipal

96

Complex (which includes City Hall, Public Works, Cabot Waterworks, and Council Chambers).
This will also provide key connection points for future projects planned along Kerr Station Road.
Attention is called to the attached Preliminary Alignment Exhibit demonstrating the
interconnection between this project, existing pedestrian routes, and future proposed
pedestrian routes.

ENTERTAINMENT DISTRICT FOR THE CITY OF CABOT, ARKANSAS, AND FOR
OTHER PURPOSES was read by City Clerk/Treasurer Tammy Yocom. Motion to suspend
the second and third reading by Mr. Davis, second by Ms. Naquin. Mr. Warner voiced his
opposition to waiving the second & third reading. Others agreed. Bob Miller, 17 Broadmoor
Circle, addressed the council in favor of an Arts and Entertainment District, but seeking a
Public Hearing on the issue to allow more citizen input. He stated he knew of people
opposed. Mr. Miller voiced his opposition to the current proposed location. Mayor Kincade
asked Mr. Miller if any of the people opposed were in attendance. They were not. Discussion.
Mr. Potts addressed the council pursuing caution in adopting this ordinance quickly. Mr.
Warner expressed his opposition to the location. It was determined there has already been
multiple public discussions, as well as, numerous surveys conducted seeking citizen input.
Mr. Long questioned the legislation being an ordinance instead of a resolution. Discussion.
Mr. Warner questioned why the name had to be changed from the already designated Central
Business District. Discussion. Motion passed 7-1 by a Roll Call Vote. Mr. Warner voted no.
Motion to adopt by Mr. Davis second by Ms. Naquin. Motion passed 6-2 by a Roll Call
Vote. Mr. Waymack and Mr. Warner voted no.

MAYORAL PROCLAMATION
Honoring Wyatt Kernodle Eagle Scout Recipient

WHEREAS: the mission of the Boy Scouts of America is to prepare young people to make ethical and
moral choices over their lifetimes by instilling in them the values of the Scout Oath and Law; and

WHEREAS: the designation of Eagle Scout is the highest achievement in the Boy Scouting program,
which was founded in 1911 over 100 hundred years ago and only four percent of Boy Scouts are granted
this distinguished rank; and

WHEREAS: Wyait Kernodle, a member of Boy Scout Troop 201 here in Cabot, Arkansas, has completed
the requirements, and was examined by the Eagle Scout Board of Review which found him worthy of the
rank of Eagle Scout on March 27, 2019; and

WHEREAS: the Boy Scouts of America encourage Eagle Scout candidates to complete worthy projects
to improve their neighborhoods and their communities; and

WHEREAS: Wyatt's Eagle Scout project included writing a proposal, having it approved, planned the
design/ayout, and coordinated donations and volunteers and led a group project to paint educational
games on the blacktop area near the playgrounds at Stagecoach Elementary School in Cabot. They
created areas to count by tens, a clock face/bullseye, a number key pad, and repainted the 4 square
game pads and other areas. This project provided a place for students to play and learn outdoors; and

WHEREAS: Wyatt Kernodle serves as an example to the youth of our community through his high level
of personal achievement, leadership and community service while being in National Honor Society,
Student Council, Thespians, and National Art honor Society at the Cabot High School, and has made the
City of Cabot very proud.

NOW, THEREFORE, I, Ken Kincade, Mayor of the City of Cabot, do hereby recognize and congratulate
Wyatt Kernodie for his outstanding accomplishment and extend to him our deepest appreciation for all of
his dedicated work and wish him the best in ail of his future endeavors as he pursues his education at the
University of Arkansas to major in Architecture and continues to be involved with the community and
scouting.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, | have hereunto set my hand and caused the Seal of the City of Cabot,
Arkansas to be affixed this 20" day of May, 2019.

ORDINANCE NO. __ OF 2019
AN ORDINANCE LEVYING AN TAX UPON THE SALE OF CERTAIN ALCOHOL
BEVERAGE SALES IN THE CITY OF CABOT; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
WHEREAS, the Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration, Alcoholic
Beverage Control Board (the “ABC) has issued permits for certain private clubs in the City of
Cabot authorizing the sale of mixed drinks and beer and wine; and
WHEREAS, Arkansas Code Ann. § 3-9-223 provides for a supplemental tax of ten percent
(10%) upon gross proceeds or gross receipts derived from private clubs for charges to members
for the preparation and serving of mixed drinks or for the cooling and serving of beer and wine,
drawn from private stocks of members of the said private clubs;
WHEREAS, Arkansas Code Ann. §3-9-223 (f) provides that city in which the premises
permitted by the ABC may impose an additional permit fee or tax, or both an additional permit fee
or supplemental tax, not to exceed one-half (1/2) of the amount of the fee or rate provided to the
State of Arkansas.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS THAT:
SECTION 1: A Supplemental Tax Upon the Sale of Certain Beverages; Pursuant to the
Ark. Code ANN. § 3-9-223 (f), as may be amended from time to time, there is levied a
supplemental tax of five (5) percent upon gross proceeds or gross receipts derived from a private
club licensed or permitted by the State of Arkansas from the charges to the members for the
preparation and serving of mixed drinks, for the cooling and serving of such beer and wine drawn
from the private stocks of such members or otherwise provided for consumptions.
SECTION 2: The city’s supplemental beverage tax is in addition to the state supplemental
tax on private clubs and shall be paid to the City Clerk/Treasurer’s Office, shall be due monthly at
the same time that the state supplemental tax is due, and shall be accompanied by one copy of the
state supplemental tax return. If any permittee shall fail to remit the supplemental tax within the
time period that the state tax is due, a penalty of 10% of the tax due shall be due and payable in
addition to the tax.
