Christmas Parade. He mentioned that this year it would be on Saturday December 7th at 5:00 and would be a lighted parade.
Clint McGue mentioned that Billy Johnson’s resolution was approved by the commission, but that he was not approved by the
governing body. So now we have an open seat on the A&P board of commissioners, and members need to come up with a
recommendation to be submitted to the council to be voted on. It needs to be someone in the tourist industry, being hotel or
restaurant. Tommy asked the commissioners to be thinking of some names and to email them prior to September’s meeting and they
would vote on them.

The A&P delinquencies continue to look better.

CITY OF CABOT, ARKANSAS
Special Council Meeting Minutes
September 23, 2019

Call to Order

Mayor Ken Kincade called to order a special meeting of the Cabot City Council at
6:30 p.m. on September 23, 2019 in the Cabot City Annex Council Chambers.

Roll Call
A roll call was conducted. The following persons were present: Council Members
Matt Webber, Ronald Waymack, Doug Warner, Ed Long, Norma Naquin, Kevin
Davis, James Reid and Damon Bivins. Also in attendance were Mayor Ken
Kincade, and City Clerk & Treasurer Tammy Yocom.

Opening Prayer by Council Member Kevin Davis.
Pledge of Allegiance by Council Member Matt Webber.

Motion to accept Jimmy Taylor’s retirement by Mr. Long, second by Ms. Naquin.
Motion passed unanimously by a Roll Call Vote.

Motion to go into Executive Session (to discuss the appointment of the City Attorney
vacancy) by Mr. Long, second by Mr. Webber. Motion passed unanimously by a Roll
Call Vote.

All in attendance, except Mayor Kincade and the eight Council Members, left the
Council Chambers at 6:34 p.m.

At 6:49 p.m., the Executive Session ended and all in attendance were allowed back into
the Council Chambers.

Motion to appoint Ben Hooper as City Attorney by Mr. Davis, second by Ms. Naquin.
Motion passed unanimously by a Roll Call Vote.

Mr. Hooper addressed the Council announcing he was happy to accept the appointment
and wanted all to know he was obligated at his current position for 30 days.

Adjournment - There being no further business, the meeting was adjourned at 6:52 p.m.
with a motion by Mr. Long, second by Mr. Waymack.

We, the undersigned Mayor and City Clerk/Treasurer for the City of Cabot, do hereby certify
the foregoing to be a true and correct record of the proceedings of the City of Cabot Special
Meeting held on Monday, September 23, 2019 at 6:30 p.m.

Clerk Janice Johnson and Deputy City Clerk Lisa Milam. Immediately following this meeting, there
is a Special Council Meeting scheduled.

Ed Long, Chairman of the Public Works Committee, called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m.

Council Member Norma Naquin: “Mr. Chairman, do you mind if | have the floor? Here's what |
would like to say and this is not pointing fingers at anyone at all. Don't take it that way at least.
..We had a committee meeting on the 25"; a Municipal Services Committee Meeting. We had
nothing on the agenda; nothing at all. And, | understand things come up. Emergencies, |
understand. But, some of the stuff that's in there was the emails were dated like October 1... |
don't understand why nothing was on our agenda and we couldn't discuss it at committee to
come up (from) committee level like it should to the Workshop Agenda...We don't need
legislation...We don't even need legislation now. It's not a committee. This is not a city council
meeting. It's a workshop. All we need is the meat of it. | mean, this is a workshop meeting; an
informal meeting.” Discussion. Mayor Kincade stated the October 1% emails arrived after the
meeting in September. Norma: “so is it an emergency that we have to have it now? Can it not go
up the normal channels?... I'm just saying like, | feel like everything's bypassing our committee
meetings, like we should do.” Discussion. Norma further discussed Adam Nobles’ appointment
by stating he would be an official with the City and Laura (his wife) works for the City. She asked
if an ordinance would have to be adopted for him to be able to do “services with the City.”
Discussion. Mayor Kincade called on City Attorney Ben Hooper who stated “my ultimate opinion
is that you do not have to do an ordinance.” Again, Norma stated “this could have been discussed
at committee...” Mayor Kincade asked “how many council members show up for the committee
meetings?” Norma made several references to the meeting on the 25" or 26" that was not
advertised and nothing was on the agenda so no one attended. She also acknowledged that
Mayor Kincade “can put anything you want on the agenda at any time”. Discussion. Ed Long: “So
then, did your committee vett the nominee? (Speaking to Matt Webber) Did y'all have a meeting

under the advice of the city attorney than | guess | need to address my question to the city
attorney....should the council not have the nominees ahead of time to be able to ask questions
and to vett them and to make sure there's not any issues? | mean, I'd like to know why we don't
do that. If it's not important for us to do it; | mean, you nominate and we appoint. It’s just that
simple.” Mayor Kincade: “that’s what we are doing here, Ed. It is two weeks before council
(meeting).” Discussion. Ed Long: “I think there is some sore spots that need to be worked out on
some things and | hope maybe that we can get that done. | think there's a breakdown in

Municipal Services: (Ed Long)

1. North Interchange Lighting Project- Joe Gunderman distributed a map (attached) of the
North Interchange and explained “you'll notice on here, there's pretty much, in the
middle of this, there is a section that is just solid black lines on both sides of 67/167. The
solid line represents what is existing on the on and off ramp lighting on the North
Interchange project. Back in, | can’t think the exact day, there was a change order for this
project, to the tune of, Tammy correct me if I’m wrong, around $517,000 for lighting of
the North Interchange. Up until this point, | believe a lot of people were under the
impression that $517,000 represented working lights. What the $517,000 change order
actually represents is 27 lights and the connectivity with them. What's missing is the
electric from the beginning source, which is down on 367 and 38 and up on the top of
Willie Ray. What's missing is from there to the source points at the bridge. Basically what
it boils down to is kind of in layman's terms here, | guess. It's like wiring your house for
electric but never putting the meter to the pole...That’s what is represented here from
the quote from L.E.G. and also from Entergy. | believe, it is roughly around a total of
around $85,000 to complete the East side. The West side, the mayor and | will work with
L.E.G. and Entergy and we're getting that side hooked up...The East side we're having to
go 2,200 feet. The original plan was to go a little over 3,000 feet aerial. To go aerial, we
would have had anywhere from a 30 to 50 foot wide easement a little over 3000 feet
long... across that middle section, that big 60 something acre tract of land that was just
rezoned. That would have put a strip of land across there that you basically can't develop
can't do anything on. The aerial lines would have ended up having to be relocated when
development comes in. If we ever light those sidewalks which ...when development
comes in we will, we would have had extensive and very expensive cost getting from the
aerial to those sidewalk lines. We met with ArDOT. We met with Entergy and we're doing
a distribution line, not a transmission line. So, the state of Arkansas will allow us to put
this electric underground within that state right of way because it is solely distribution
from this point. Entergy has also agreed that the four inch conduit could be used at a
future date for future developments. So, that's an economic development incentive to
the development of that area that they would not have that added expense. We have
worked with L.E.G. and Entergy and, instead of doing two four inch conduits, Entergy is
okay with doing a four inch and a two inch, which basically knocks about 20 grand off of
the price of this. And Entergy has not gotten me a solid number. That $24,900 and some
change is based off of a March 2019 estimated quote. | spoke with Sean Hollingshead
today and he said that he has got the quote ready, but he can't get it prepared. They're
having computer issues. But, he said that it has actually decreased from that $24,900.
Now, their price has come down, L.E.G’s price has come down, and that has taken a lot of

Contract to do Business with Neel-Schaffer (Phase II) — Joe Gunderman: “The City's got an
agreement to contract with Neel-Schaffer for a ... signal system upgrade project that we
do have some State and Federal funding on. Back on July 16 of 2018, Resolution 17 of
2018 authorized the Mayor and City Clerk to execute any documents necessary to
contract with Neel-Schaffer... This project is basically two projects in one. Phase | was what
was called .... the Systems Engineering Analysis, which was basically Neel-Schaffer and
their engineering team coming in and doing a full evaluation assessment of our current
inventory; what we got; where it is; how it functions; and then, get that to ARDot with
kind of a plan to switch everything from what it is now to an adaptive traffic system. And,
what that means is the signals at Rockwood and 89 would talk to the signal in 367 and 89
to better communicate how traffic is flowing at one point in town to get to the other point
in town better. That was Phase |. They got that Systems Engineering Analysis to ARDot.
ArDot approved everything and this is where we got into Phase II. Phase II is basically
Neel-Schaffer taking the project from design and engineering phases, through the
bidding, through the bid award, through the construction, through the project
management, through final; everything turnkey, A to Z, ready to go. The problem that we
came to find out when it came time to do Phase II: | had sent Jimmy Taylor, back to July,
all of this to review. And, his opinion was that this was an extension, or it was a
continuation of the already entered into agreement. Again, we got to do a little bit more
research on this. | got with Tammy. | got with the mayor. And, the way that this resolution
was written, the resolution references Phase | and Il in the amount of $67,312.74. But
when you get to digging through the 64 page contract, it references Phase | at $67,300.74.
But, it goes through that contract listing all of the details and everything of Phase II that
has to be done after Phase |. Again, there's a missing part there. It never referenced the
amount of Phase Il. Phase | of $67,312.74 was solely the Systems Engineering and Analysis
Report. Neel-Schaffer did not use all of that funding; they only use the 67% of it. But Phase
Il, which is pretty much designing it, submitting it, getting it approved, doing the bid docs,
getting the bids, doing the bid award, project management; everything all turn key is
$106,000 and some change. Come find out that we need to come to the council to get
this language cleaned up, so to speak, to where everything is not misconstrued, not any
issues. And, like | said, the 64 page contract outlines Phase Il. And it says that, upon
completion of Phase I, Neel-Schaffer shall continue to do the components for Phase Il,
but it never references that amount. There was some left out language in the Resolution
17 of 2018. Discussion. Motion to place this item on this month’s Council Meeting Agenda
by Damon, second by Kevin. Motion passed unanimously.

TO EXECUTE ANY DOCUMENTS NECESSARY TO ENTER INTO A CONTRACT

waiving the current procedures for selection of professional services, established by Ordinance
No 55 of 2003, to allow for the request for qualifications for traffic signal engineering design
services; and

selection group individually evaluated each qualification and has determined Neel-Schaffer, Inc
to be the most qualified engineer firm for the project; and
WHEREAS, the City and Neel-Schaffer, Inc have negotiated the costs and terms of Phase
II of the Traffic Signal Engineering Design Services, which is explained in more detail in Exhibit
“A” attached hereto and incorporated herein by this reference, and the City desires to move
forward with implementation of Phase II in the amount of One Hundred Six Thousand, Six
Hundred Eighty-Eight Dollars and 38/100 Cents ($106,688.38); subject to the approval of this
governing body.
NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS, THAT:
SECTION 1: The Mayor and City Clerk~Treasurer are hereby authorized to execute any
and all documents necessary to enter into a Contract with Neel-Schaffer, Inc, for Traffic Signal
Engineering Design Services.
SECTION 2: The agreed upon cost for Traffic Signal Engineering Design Services is in
the amount One Hundred Six Thousand, Six Hundred Eighty-Eight Dollars and 38/100 Cents
($106,688.38) and is hereby approved.
SECTION 3: This resolution shall be in full force and effect from and after its passage.

TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION OF BASIC PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
PHASE 2 - SYSTEM SOFTWARE AND INTERSECTION DESIGN, CONTRACT
DOCUMENTS AND BID/AWARD
PROJECT MANAGEMENT AND COORDINATION
The project will be managed following all applicable City, ArDOT and FHW A methods and procedures, as
well as following all necessmy Local Programs requirements by ArDOT. At the beginning of the project and
with the onset of each task, the Engineer will hold a kick-off meeting with the City and ArDOT to formulate
a clear understanding of the project plans requirements, including discussion of submittals, advertisement
and procurement. This meeting will include discussion of the project scope, schedule, communication
protocol, and team organization to move the design and Signal System Synchronization vendor phases
forward on a timely basis.
Project progress meetings for this task will routinely be conducted by teleconference (or on site) to
provide detailed updates on the project status. These meetings will occur as needed, but no less often than
monthly. Further reference to these meetings can be found in the specific task descriptions below. The
Engineer will prepare agendas for and schedule all meetings with concurrence of the City's Project
Manager and will distribute meeting minutes afterward.
Monthly status repo1ts will be prepared by the Engineer that cover the project progress from one report to
the next and will indicate the work completed during the past month. These monthly repmts will most
often accompany the monthly progress billing.
ENVIRONMENTAL DOCUMENTS
The Engineer will prepare the necessmy environmental documents to be submitted to ArDOT /FHW A.
Typically, this type project with minimal constrnction and no environmental impact as well as no right of way
issues would be documented as a Categorical Exclusion Type project. The Engineer will coordinate the matter
with ArDOT and Metroplan.

SIGNAL SYSTEM SYNCHRONIZATION SOFTWARE, HARDWARE AND NETWORK
SERVER
The signal software would be procured either by a 'best value' type procurement, or through sole
source procurement.
Initially the Engineer will meet with the City and ARDOT to determine if a sole source procedure
would be acceptable for this project and what would be required to meet FHW A guidelines for sole
source procurement process. If this method is possible, then equipment specifications and other
software requirements would be developed and submitted to the sole source vendor for costing and
delive1y and negotiations with the City.
If the procurement method is to be a 'best value' type of procurement, the software would be selected
based on technical evaluation through a Request for Proposal (RFP) fonnat on how well the software
vendor meets and answers the requirements stated in the RFP and the needs statements as per the
approved System Engineering Analysis Report.
-1-

The RFP would consist of equipment specifications and other criteria for an off-the-shelf type
software for city-wide master signal synchronization purpose as well as the manner of
communications with the intersections including antennas for broadband co1mnunications if
necessary mounted on the radio tower at City Hall. After procurement selection, cost of the software
would then be negotiated with the City and a contract would be executed. The contract would include
software vendor services, including configuration, training, testing and suppo1i. The Engineer will
work with the City in performing the RFP review and rankings but will not have a vote in the
selection. The City will need to provide at least three (3) City employees to review and rank the
submitted RFPs.
Additionally, any vendor requirements for support and integration of the system, including
conditional and final acceptance testing requirements and also annual support. Any required
training and documentation desired by the City will be part of the RFP requirements.
Engineer will meet with the City's IT department to dete1mine how to incorporate the signal system
master software/server on the existing city computer system via a network server. Vendors may also
want to meet with the IT department and view the City's computer network setup. Any requirement for
coordination with the City's IT department for installation of the network server and software will be
included in either the sole source or RFP type procurement method. Installation of the server and
software will done in direct communication and oversite by the City's IT department. This will include
any coordination necessary for providing intersection communications to the network server/master .
INTERSECTION DESIGN - LOW BID PROCESS
DESIGN PLANS AND TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS
The Engineer shall provide engineering design services for the preparation o f the signal
modifications including detection/communications plans and specifications. The design plans will be
developed using the Local Agency Technical Standards of ArDOT, and per City requirements, and
all other applicable standards as required. For this scope, it is intended that the Plans shall include
nine (9) signalized intersection layouts at the following locations:
•
•
•

2nd St (Hwy 367) at Elm St, Main/Pine St, and Locust St(3)
Main St (Hwy 89) at Going Dr., Dakota St. and 10 th St. (3)
Pine St (Hwy 89) at Lincoln St, Campground Rd and Panther Trail (3)

Signal Intersection Improvements may include new controllers, MMU's, video detection, Flashing
Yell ow arrow phasing, controller modifications, broadband and cellular communications to the
master, antennas, PTZ cameras and video processors, and possibly batte1y power back-ups.
The Engineer shall submit 60%, 90% and Final plan sets per ArDOT minimum requirements. It is
not expected that any more plans submittals than these will be required. While no new signals will be
designed for this project, all applicable standards and guidance in this Chapter will be used for any
new detection or devices required. The intersection plan layout sheets shall be derived from existing
pdf and CAD drawings supplied by the ArDOT and/or the City from past ITS, signal or intersection
improvement projects. Survey and geotechnical data gathering is not included in this scope. The
intersection plan layout sheets shall show existing features and detection, along with new detection
types and their location. Any other new devices or features required by the ASCT, such as
communications, cabling, or other detection, shall be shown on the plans and detail sheets. Detail
-2-

sheets shall include all requirements for the chosen detection, including notes, manufacturer
installation requirements and drawings. The Engineer shall work with the signal system
synchronization vendor, awarded the software contract, in regard to any communications or detection
specifications required by the manufacturer, for the bid document.
The plans will include these sheets:
• Title
• Index
• General Notes
• Summary o f Quantities
• Recap of Quantities
• SystemMap
• Each intersection to include a detail plan sheet and a sheet of charts, wiring and phasing
diagram and intersection notes.
• Equipment detail installation sheets
• Standard Traffic Control Sheets

BIDs AND AW ARDs.
Two separate bid packages will include all items in this Task of work, the RFP selected by technical
selection committee and a Low Bid Signal modification plan set for nine intersections.
The first bid package shall be for the signal system synchronization software procurement.
The second bid package will be for a Signal Modification Contract that will utilize an experienced
signal installation contractor that will utilize the plans for installation of the required devices.
The City will be responsible for the cost to advertise the projects in statewide newspapers as legal
notices.
The Engineer will prepare documents for the two bid packages, which shall include:
Assistance in selection of the Signal System Synchronization software/hardware vendor
Bid documents using standard City Contract language, as required
Standard City Contract to be used to award the contract to the approved software vendor and
approved low bidder.
Assist the City in advertising and bidding both bid documents
Attend any pre-bid meetings and be available for questions and clarifications prior to the bid opening
The Engineer will assist the City in getting the contracts to the Vendor/Contractor for execution and
submittal back to the City for City Board approvals and in coordinating the effort with ArDOT for
authorization by ArDOT in acceptance of the bids and in obtaining notices to proceed.

GUESTS PRESENT: Travis Young with Parks & Rec., Clint McGue, legal counsel, Gina Jones, Gina Quattlebaum, AmyWilliams with

Tommy Hignight called the meeting to order at 8:32 a.m.

Minutes- The Commissioners reviewed the minutes for the August 2019 meeting. Motion to approve was made by Jay Lallu, with
Brian Knowles making the second. The commission voted. August 2019 minutes were approved.
Financial Report- The Commission reviewed the August 2019 financial report. Ed Long made a motion to approve the financial
report, with Jay Lallu making the second. The financial report for August 2019 was approved.
Funding Recap- Jeff Melton with Rolling Hills Country Club was here on behalf of the Randy Beaver Memorial Golf Tournament
recap. He said that it was a great success and that they had 55 golfers with Blain Calhoun from Cabot winning the tournament.
Each participant got golf balls and a towel. They got a lot of great feedback. He was very grateful to the A&P for helping to fund
the event.
Chamber Report – Amy Williams stated that the air force ball that the A&P helped to fund was this past Saturday and that it was a
great night. Mickey Spillane brought by a certificate of appreciation for the A&P funding the Arkansas Freedom Fund. Economic
Development wise, we are working to get the lights up and running at the new interchange. The hospital keeps pushing back
opening day due to some health department items that must be done. Starbucks is now open. We have 7 or 8 projects in the works
right now and things are going well. We had two ribbon cuttings yesterday and one today at Chef Candace at 11:00.
Gina Quattlebaum was here to talk about how busy things have been with Cabotfest. It will be on October 12 th. Carnival will kick
off on the 10th. We will host battle of the bands on Friday night this year and we are still looking for bands to participate. Little
Kato will also be here wrestling to defend his world championship title. We will be kicking off this year at 10:00 instead of 9:00
with our big entertainment being “Unspoken” and they will kickoff at 7:00 pm on Saturday October 12 th. We will also have “Stars
Go Dim” and “Katie Hurst”. The treasure hunt will be Oct 1 through October 12 th with our grand prize winner that will be drawn
on the stage on the 12th
Cabot Parks & Rec – Travis Young was here. He said that the city finalized the turf loan this past week. They will start making
payments on that loan next month. The turf production is about 80% complete. They will start on the baseball fields hopefully next
week. Fall sports is up about 100 people and is going great. Center memberships are starting to creep up again as well. Winter
sports registration has kicked off. We have a local physical therapist that is going to be doing an event about shoulder pain at the
event center. On September 23rd, the health department is doing a mass flu clinic at the event center.
General Discussion- Tommy Hignight said that he has received 4 names as possible candidates to fill the open A&P seat. He will
contact them and see if they might be interested. He told the commission that if they had any other names, to send them his way.
Clint McGue mentioned there is a business that we continue to have issues with them not paying their taxes and he requested that
we vote to revoke their license. He said that they will have a time period where they can appeal this before the commission. He
feels that they will come in and get them caught up or make arrangements so that they won’t have to close. He said that if they
don’t ask for anything, to be aware that we will be shutting down the restaurant.
Motion to revoke the A&P permit was made by: JayLallu
2nd was made by Tommy Hignight and it passed

The next A&P meeting will be October 15, 2019.

Cabot Parks and Recreation Commission Meeting
October 15, 2019
Cabot Veterans Park Meeting Room
508 North Lincoln, Cabot, Arkansas 72023

I.

Call to Order/Roll Call
John C. Thompson called the meeting to order at 6:32 pm.
Present: Greg Sled, Mike Nash, Matt Moudy, John C. Thompson, Tricia Ambeau, Adam Noble
Maggie Cope.

II.

Minutes of Regular Meeting
The minutes of the regular meeting held on September 17, 2019 were presented. MATT
MOUDY MOTIONED TO ACCEPT THE MINTES OF SEPTEMBER 17, 2019, SECOND BY GREG
SLED, ALL VOTED AYE.
Financials

III.

September 2019 financials were presented. General Director Travis Young stated that the utility fees
have decreased due to the installation of digital meters. The community center’s meter has not yet
been replaced. The new website with CivicPlus is currently being structured and will include ADA access
to the site. The company specializes in Government operations. Pool chemical expenses are high due
the high temperatures in September. Overtime wages will be paid out in October. Grants will be paid
out soon and will decrease the current revenue over $100,000.00. Commission Tricia Ambreau asked it
was possible to include the Spanish language on the website. Concession revenue is a little off due to
the large amount of back stock. GREG SLED MOTIONED TO ACCEPT THE FINANCIALS AS PRESENTED,
SECOND BY MATT MOUDY, ALL VOTED AYE.

IV.

Programs
Program Director Lorenzo Mendoza stated that registration for youth wrestling is being held
with 62 already registered in the program. Basketball registering is also registering currently.
The programs are now a member of National Alliance of Youth Sports. Unfortunately, the
competitive league will not be played due to lack of participants. Staff met with coaches from
the high school to make some changes on rules to comply with USA basketball standards and
have the coaches hold some clinics for volunteer coaches.
Football – Only a couple of weeks left with the Super Bowl scheduled November 9 th. Overall
this was a good season.
Flag Football – No report. Lorenzo will reach out the association for a report.

103

Youth Cheer – Everything is going well with better communication with youth football.
Commission Tricia Ambreau asked if the group had accommodations for special needs
individuals.
BMX – Heather Phillips presented the report. They are down to the last two months of the
season and are seeing an increase in riders. Races are held every Thursday evening and on
Saturday’s. Soil Tack has been applied on one stretch. The entire track has not been put down
yet but will be done soon weather permitting.
General Director Travis Young explained the working relationship between the parks and the
associations to the new members of the commission.
V.

Construction/Facility Update
General Director Travis Young gave an update on the bike trails proposed at Cabot Regional
Park. The International Mountain Bike will do a site visit on 11/19/19. Mr. Young suggested
that the parks hold a public meeting on that same day to allow citizens to ask questions while
the group was in town.
Stage 1 of 3 has be completed on the baseball fields with the installation of the turf. Progress
going well and weather permitting, the grid system will be put in place.
The Aquatic park ended the season with the Doggie Dive with 68 dogs taking part. The pool
was drained and the last of the leaks has been repaired.
Over seeding on the football fields has started.
October 29th Travis Young will meet with the grant committee involving the project on Richie
Road.

VI.

Old Business
None
New Business
Field Donation – The park department was approached about waiving field rental fees for a
benefit tournament. The fields are under construction to install the artificial turf and the
commissions feels that it would not be in the best interest of all involved to approve rental on
fields that may not be ready for play. Using tax dollars to pay expenses for a benefit
tournament was discussed. The commissions suggested looking at other park departments as
to how they handle such requests.

VII.

104

VIII.

IX.

General Director Travis Young asked for commission members to volunteer to serve on the
budget committee. John C. Thompson, Nick Whitaker, and Tricia Ambeau will serve on this
committee.
Community Input
Matt Webber spoke on behave of Cabot City Beautiful and the Lions Club to thank the staff of
Cabot Parks and Recreation for “bending over backwards” to help the groups anytime they are

My central reason for vetoing the ordinance was the undue economic burden it places on
the citizens of Cabot. If the ordinance were to take effect the minimum monthly payment would
rise and would continue to rise until it reaches a 48% increase for most customers by 2022. In
addition, the price per 1,000 gallons after the minimum payment threshold is reached would be
increased by 47% for most customers immediately upon the rates going into effect and would
continue to climb to 140% by 2022. To support such a substantial increase, the Commission
offered a single central justification: asset depreciation. However, the Commission’s own
audited financial statements for 2017 and 2018 only show total wastewater asset depreciation at
24.8%. That is not nearly enough to justify such a substantial rate increase over such a short
amount of time. This is especially true given the assets the Commission already has on hand.
According to their own 2017/2018 financial statements they have $4,345,596 in unrestricted
cash assets. A 140% rate increase is clearly unreasonable when the Commission is sitting on
such substantial cash assets.

These concerns are especially troubling as the ordinance (that the Commission itself
drafted) does not provide for any transparency at all on how the Commission will spend the
extra revenue. Not only does the ordinance not require the Commission to actually use the extra
revenue to offset asset depreciation, it imposes no usage requirements, limitations, or
accountability at all. The ordinance would give the Commission carte blanche to use the extra
revenue however it sees fit with no word of explanation as to where the money is actually going.
For a lesser rate increase and for more justifiable reasons this issue of accountability on usage
may not be as troubling. But in this case, given the Commission’s 4.3 million in cash on hand,
the lack of transparency is especially concerning, and it is not at all unreasonable to require the
Commission to explain to the people of Cabot where their money is going.

While it is likely true, as the Council stated, that many Cabot families would be able to
absorb the impact of the rate increase, it is also true that it will not be nearly so simple for our
city’s less advantaged families. It is undeniable that for our economically struggling families an
ultimate rate increase of 140% would be an added financial burden. I believe that the
Commission has completely failed to justify why such a burden to those families is necessary,
especially in light of the over 4.3 million dollars of cash assets it already has on hand.

As an additional matter, I also have concerns regarding the Commission’s diligence in
raising this issue and acting on it. Councilman Warner stated at the November 4" Work Session
that this matter had been discussed all the way back in 2012: “...if you go back to 2012. It was
addressed then that the rate would need to be increased.” Why then is this only now — 7 years
later — being brought before the Council? If true, it certainly appears that the Commission has
acted irresponsibly on this issue. It is possible that past city administrations bear some blame
here as well, but — if this 7 year delay is accurate — the clear and obvious conclusion is that the
Commission has not acted diligently in this matter. Given this lack of diligence and
responsibility on behalf of the Commission, it is all the more important that the ordinance
provide for transparency on how the extra revenue will actually be spent.

I fully appreciate that at some point Wastewater rates will need to be raised and I would
not be opposed to a rate increase as long as: the rate of increase in reasonable; there is sufficient
need on behalf of the Commission; and if there is transparency as to how the extra revenue will
actually be spent. However, it is my firm opinion that the Wastewater Commission has not met
its burden in showing that such a significant increase over such a short amount of time is
warranted. The Commission is sitting on over 4.3 million dollars of unrestricted cash assets and
yet they are asking for the people of Cabot to offset their 24.8% depreciation with an eventual
rate increase of 140%. For all these reasons I find that Ordinance 18 of 2019 is clearly contrary

to the public interest.

RE:

Competitive Bid Waiver Request

Distinguished Members of the Council,
Attached to this month's Council Packet is a request to waive competitive bids for the purchase of 12
portable, hand-held radios for use at the Cabot Fire Department. These radios will aid the replacement
of outdated and unsupported radios that we are currently using. The purchase will be from a state bid
contract and from a "sole source" vendor.
Our current models of Motorola XTS 2500 have been in service in excess of 15 years. These radios are no
longer supported by Motorola for maintenance. This means they are no longer making replacement
parts and as radios break, the cost to repair is ever increasing. The frequency of repairs is increasing as
radios age.
Communications play a vital role in on-scene safety for our first-line crews. With the purchase of these
12 portable radios, our firefighters will have greater reliability when they need it most. The department
and City will have more sustainable resources that will be supported through the 2030 timeframe.
These radios are being purchased from Motorola direct and are priced at a state bid contracted price.
The radios are costly at around $4,700/each. We are trading in 12 of our older radios and receiving
additional corporate discounts to drive the cost down as much as possible.
Thank you, in advance, for your time and consideration.

Dwayne Boswell

Cabot City Council Work Session
Cabot City Annex / Council Chambers
December 2, 2019
6:30 p.m.

The Cabot City Council held its monthly Work Session on Monday, November 4, 2019 in the City
Annex Council Chambers. Council members present were: Ed Long, James Reid, Damon Bivins,
Ronald Waymack, Doug Warner, Kevin Davis, Norma Naquin and Matt Webber. Others present:
Mayor Ken Kincade, City Attorney Ben Hooper, City Clerk & Treasurer Tammy Yocom, Deputy City
Clerk Lisa Milam and Deputy City Clerk Janice Conway-Johnson.

Ed Long, Chairman of the Municipal Services Committee, called the meeting to order at 6:30
p.m.

1. Gold Award Project - Abigail Evans, Cabot High School student, explained her desire to
partner with Cabot Parks & Rec for her Girl Scout Gold Award project. She proposes to
provide totes filled with camping supplies for others to “check out” as needed through
Parks & Rec. No action.

2. Support Replacement of Half-Cent Sales Tax — Discussion. Motion to place item on this
month’s Council Meeting Agenda by Kevin, second by Matt. Motion passed with a 7-0-1
vote. Doug Warner abstained from voting.

3. Municipal Services Community Input — City Attorney Ben Hooper addressed the council
with information regarding the recent rezone request for 68 S. Pine Street. Ben
announced that legally the council can take it (the rezone request) up themselves and act
on this without the Planning Commission when an emergency exists which threatens the
health, safety, welfare and morals of the citizens of the city. He suggested they make a
case for the emergency and set a precedent as to why they are considering the rezone
this time and not every case that comes up. Discussion. Ben also advised that financial
considerations cannot be the sole basis for an emergency. There has to be another
legitimate factor that goes with it. This information was provided in consideration of the
upcoming Council Meeting on December 16". Discussion.

The meeting was turned over to Damon Bivins, Chairman of the Police & Fire Committee at 6:44
p.m.

1. Purchase of Hand Held Radios for Fire Department — Discussion. Motion to place item on
this month’s Council Meeting Agenda by Kevin, second by Ed. Motion passed with a
unanimous vote.

2. Motion by Ed to have the purchase of the Fire Department’s Quick Response Vehicle on
this month’s Council Meeting Agenda, second by Norma. Motion passed with a
unanimous vote.

3. Police & Fire Community Input — None

The meeting was turned over to Doug Warner, Chairman of the Budget & Personnel Committee
at 6:53 p.m.

--- page 2 (OCR) ---
1. Cabot Housing Authority Re-Appointment — David Hipp — Discussion. Motion to place item
on this month’s Council Meeting Agenda by Damon, second by James. Motion passed with
a unanimous vote.

2. 2020 Proposed Operating Budget — Discussion. It was determined there will be a special
meeting on December 10" at 6:30 p.m. to discuss the proposed budget. No action.

3. Budget & Personnel Committee Input - None

The meeting was turned over to Kevin Davis, Chairman of the Community Development
Committee at 7:00 p.m.

1. No items on Agenda
2. Community Development Community Input — Amy Williams gave a brief update on
community development.

The meeting was turned over to Ron Waymack, Chairman of the Military Affairs Committee at
7:07 p.m.

1. No items on Agenda
2. Military Affairs Committee Community Input - None

Meeting was adjourned at 7:09 p.m. by a unanimous vote.

RESOLUTION NO. 30 of 2019
A RESOLUTION BY THE CITY OF CABOT, ARKANSAS SUPPORTING THE HOUSE
JOINT RESOLUTION 1018 OF 2019 (HJR 1018 OF 2019), PROPOSING AN
AMENDMENT TO THE ARKANSAS CONSTITUTION TO CONTINUE A LEVY OF A
ONE-HALF PERCENT SALES AND USE TAX FOR STATE HIGHWAYS AND
BRIDGES; COUNTY ROADS, BRIDGES, AND OTHER SURFACE TRANSPORTATION;
AND CITY STREETS, BRIDGES, AND OTHER SURFACE TRANSPORTATION AFTER
THE RETIREMENT OF THE BONDS AUTHORIZED IN ARKANSAS CONSTITUTION,
AMENDMENT 91, AS SPECIAL REVENUE TOBE DISTRIBUTED UNDER THE
ARKANSAS HIGHWAY REVENUE DISTRIBUTION LAW; AND FOR OTHER
PURPOSES
WHEREAS, Arkansas Constitution, Amendment 91, levies a one-half percent sale and use
tax to provide additional funding for the state's four-lane highway system, county roads, and city
streets; and,
WHEREAS, the one-half percent sales and use tax under Arkansas Constitution,
Amendment 91, is due to expire on June 30, 2023 unless a new constitutional amendment is
passed; and,
WHEREAS, HJR 1018 proposes that the sales and use tax levied under Arkansas
Constitution, Amendment 91, be continued to provide special revenue for use of maintaining,
repairing, and improving the state's system of highways, county roads, and city streets; and,
WHEREAS, without continuation of this sales and use tax the state will be unable to meet
the severe and pressing needs to maintain and improve the state's system of state highways,
county roads, and city streets; and,
WHEREAS, the continuation of the one-half percent sales and use tax will ensure future
investment in the state highway system, county roads, and city streets; and,
WHEREAS, this investment will create jobs, aid in economic development, improve
quality of life, and provide additional transportation infrastructure, including specifically, a fourlane highway construction plan designed to connect all regions of the state, and;
WHEREAS, it is beneficial for all municipalities to support HJR 1018 as a necessary
funding mechanism for our travel-infrastructure and will serve as an economic boon for the
State.
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT
ARKANSAS:
SECTION 1: That we do hereby support the legal proposals found in HJR 1018 of 2019,
as well as its adoption by the people of the State of Arkansas at the next general election.

CABOT ANNOUNCES DECEMBER EMPLOYEE OF THE MONTH

While each employee of the month announcement is special, this one in particular has extra importance.
Not only is this employee being recognized for his achievement over the last few months and beyond; but
for his part in helping turn an entire Department around. In addition to being named employee of the
month, this month’s winner will receive something extra.

Therefore, in front of the entire City, family, and co-workers, the City of Cabot recognizes Dwayne
Boswell as the employee of the month for December for his hard work and dedication during the month
of November and beyond. In addition, officially as of tonight, Dwayne will no longer be just the interim
Fire Chief, but the City is proud to announce him as the permanent Fire Chief.

Midway through the year, it was obvious that a major change was needed in the Fire Department.
Wanting to make the right decision and not rush to a new hire, Dwayne along with the other two Battalion
Chiefs, Louis Cimino and Jim Firebaugh, were put in charge while things were sorted out. All three of
these men took on a very difficult assignment and did an amazing job. This cannot be overstated.

As the search began for a Fire Chief, Chief Boswell stepped forward and expressed his desire to run the
Department. His vision was a Fire Department where guys felt like family again and were excited to come
to work each day. He wanted the Fire Department to be a team member of the City’s administration and
take an approach to leadership that benefits everyone. After a long search and speaking with candidates
from both locally and across the US, Chief Boswell was named the interim Chief on October 21%. In
almost two months to the day, the City is seeing the rewards of this decision.

Chief Boswell has opened things up to the Fire Department from the top to the bottom. Ideas and
suggestions are flowing and many changes have already been made. Simple things from filling shifts to
clothing options were instantaneous. In conjunction with Police, a charity kickball game was held. The
amount of off duty and on duty firefighters and their families present was impossible not to notice. As has
been publicized, the Fire Department recently raised $12,788 for their Cabot Christmas for Kids program.
Tonight’s meeting has a resolution for a quick response vehicle. Promotions were just done through
assessment centers and outside feedback. The list goes on and on. Just visiting each station and seeing the
difference of the interaction of the men and their demeanor is so difficult to put in words.

The decision to make Chief Boswell the permanent Chief was most evident though by the amount of
Firefighters who have approached the Mayor and Human Resources in the last two months. Each of them
not only shared their excitement for the new direction of the Department, but many of them kept asking
the same question: when would the interim tag be removed?

For being chosen employee of the month, he will receive a plaque with his name on it, his name added to
the list of employees chosen as employee of the month on the City Hall plaque, his story in the
newspaper, his photo and name added to the City website, and lunch or breakfast with the Mayor and the
Human Resources Director.
